title: No reward model and no critic
summary: Which alignment methods train without fitting a reward model or a value network.

choices.text: A Bradley-Terry reward model trained on the pairs, then used only to rank samples, with the policy weights left frozen.
SimPO on chosen/rejected pairs, using the length-normalized average log probability as the implicit reward and a target margin, with no reference model.
DPO on chosen/rejected pairs, with a frozen reference policy in the log-probability ratios.
KTO on unpaired thumbs-up and thumbs-down labels, with the implied reward compared to a frozen reference policy.
PPO-based RLHF, which fits a reward model on human pairs and trains a critic.
GRPO that scores a group of sampled responses with an external scalar reward and a group-normalized advantage, and trains no value network.
ORPO on chosen/rejected pairs: a supervised loss on the chosen response plus an odds-ratio penalty, with no reference model.
